messages:
sam: Noticing provisioning failures for new GPU nodes in us-west-2 after yesterday's IAM role-boundary rollout. Capacity down ~18%.

julia: saw alerts, thanks. Any logs? which step failing? :eyes:

sam: bootstrap fails at instance profile assume: "AccessDenied: sts:AssumeRole" — looks like role-boundary policy blocks the node role from assuming the provisioning service role.

matteo: that matches a policy change I merged (tighten role-boundary on service accounts). I thought only control-plane tokens would be affected but apparently node bootstrap uses the same path.

olivia: infra-bot shows 32 failed instances today in us-west-2-gpu-pool. All with error code 403 from STS.

infra-bot: Alert: 32/180 launch attempts failed in us-west-2-gpu-pool; root cause: IAM boundary enforcement change. Link: https://runbook/internal/prov-iam-rollback

sam: also noticed CloudTrail events missing for some of the failed assume-role attempts in that region — audit logs not capturing the STS denies.

julia: that's bad for compliance. Matteo, can you roll back the boundary change for the node-boot role? We need capacity ASAP and full audit trail.

matteo: rolling back now, will push a revert in 60s. keeping change ID 2026-088-restrict for traceability.

sam: switching routing to other regions while we restore, but customers on us-west facing degraded QPS. ETA for nodes to recover? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

matteo: IAM revert applied. Starting a controlled reprovision of 40 nodes (warm pool). monitor shows STS calls succeeding now.

olivia: warm pool fill triggered, but still seeing a few attach-time network errors: "ENI attach timeout" — possible VPC route table change interfering with attach calls.

julia: did any of the networking infra changes coincide with the IAM rollout? I recall a small route-table cleanup in the same PR.

matteo: hmm yes, I removed a legacy ENI route in us-west-2 during the same maintenance window. Could be related.

sam: for now keep IAM rollback, Matteo. Olivia, can you validate the ENI subnet route table and NACLs? If needed, re-add temporary route to restore attach path.

olivia: checking now. Found an implicit deny from NACL rule 140 on the gpu-subnet-eu-west (misapplied copy). Reverting NACL copy. Applying patch in 2m.

infra-bot: Deploy job 3842: NACL patch applied to gpu-subnet-us-west-2; wait for propagation ~90s.

sam: logs now show attaches succeeding and nodes coming up. Capacity recovering to ~98% after 10 minutes.

julia: good. Need postmortem and a compliance check: missing CloudTrail entries for the STS denies earlier — Matteo, why were events not ingested?

matteo: investigation: a malformed CloudTrail S3 replication rule left some events unprocessed in us-west-2 bucket. I fixed the replication and reingested backlog — events now present.

sam: action items: 1) Matteo: create PR to separate IAM boundary rollout from network changes (cherry-pick split) 2) Olivia: audit NACL copy scripts to prevent region mixups 3) Julia: run a compliance verification to confirm CloudTrail has all STS denies for the window and escalate to security if gaps remain.

olivia: noted, I'll own the NACL script PR.

matteo: will open the split-PR and add a canary (small cohort) runbook. Linking ticket INF-2026-117.

julia: I'll run compliance audit and post results here. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — keep the thread updated with any residual errors. Closing routing fallback in 2 hours if stable.

infra-bot: Incident resolved: capacity restored; root causes: IAM role-boundary combined with NACL copy bug and delayed CloudTrail ingestion. Postmortem ticket: INF-2026-117.
